The beauty of a blank canvas. I'm free to explore any idea, tangentially connected or not, and see where it takes me. 

As I ponder the idea of freedom, I'm reminded of a night in my early twenties when I hitchhiked across the Scottish Highlands. The sky was ablaze with stars, and the darkness seemed to pulse with energy. We drove along the glinting shores of Loch Ness, the wind whipping our hair into a frenzy. The music from our phones blended with the hum of the car's engine, creating an otherworldly symphony. It was a moment of pure abandon, a feeling that I'd only ever experienced a handful of times before in my life.

It got me thinking about that stranger I met at the side of the road who let us into their car. We ended up driving all night, clicking songs in with their navigation system, sharing stories about the places we'd been. No names were exchanged, but we parted ways as if sealed by a perpetual bond. 

Liberty, I suspect, stems from both inward and outward defiance. Overcoming internal narratives, limitations, or the need for validation from others. Accepting one's place within the tapestry of humanity – all complicated, amplified, and disparate threads. We secretly bake our identities in the glazed radiance of the world around us.

Free will seems malleable, its origins compete, intersect with temptation, resistance, arrogance – or pilgrimage's tested strength.
